messages:
Leah: FYI FinTechCo hitting elevated latency and intermittent 5xx since 03:12 UTC. They say traffic is egressing via APAC (SG) even though their Private VPC is in us-west-2. Billing shows increased regional egress fees. Repro steps + logs below. @Raj can you pick this up?

FinTechCo (pasted into thread): Steps to reproduce:
1) curl -w '%{time_total}s' -o /dev/null -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
2) note response time ~2.6-3s and occasional 502

They included traceroute from their on-prem jumpbox:
```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (13.54.23.11), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.245 ms
 2  198.51.100.1  1.10 ms
 5  203.80.11.1  12.1 ms
 7  139.130.1.2  48.3 ms
 9  103.12.45.2  150.7 ms
=> observed path goes via APAC edges (Singapore)
```

Also pasted the request headers they see at the proxy: 
```
:method: POST
:scheme: https
host: api.redwood.ai
x-client-region: us-west-2
x-forwarded-for: 198.51.100.22
x-redwood-egress: nat-203.80.11.1
```

Raj: I'm oncall, grabbing their NAT translation table and proxy route decisions now. Can you confirm tenant id and any recent peering work?

Leah: Tenant id 8f4c. No changes on their side per customer. They called out a spike right after 02:58 UTC.

Tess: Quick check - could be our peering route-map. If the hub that peers with them got a higher local-pref/ lower MED for APAC on overflow, failover could pick APAC NATs. Asking network ops for BGP table + recent route-map diffs.

Maya: Also saw a similar pattern last month where an edge healthcheck flapped (us-west), so the proxy pool moved traffic to APAC proxies. Two things to confirm: 1) proxy healthcheck logs 2) SNI/host-based healthcheck name resolution. Temporary mitigation: we support a region hint header `x-redwood-prefer-region: us-west` that forces routing preference for the request (documented internally). Can we ask FinTechCo to add that while we fix infra?

Leah: They can't ship a code change quickly. Any hotfix we can do from our side?

Raj: Short-term options: 1) add an explicit tenant->us-west route hint in the edge routing tier for tenant 8f4c 2) rollback the peering route-map change if it's the cause. I'm pulling NAT translations, proxy selection logs and edge health results now. Will share a diag bundle link in ~15m.

SRE-bot: Detected change: peering-policy-2026-03-12 applied at 02:58:03 UTC. Diff summary: APAC failover pref increased.

Tess: Confirmed the diff — MED decreased toward APAC for overflow prefixes. Network ops is escalating. Preparing rollback request.

Leah: Filed INC-4952 and linked FinTechCo billing spike + repro. Asked FinOps to flag potential refund if traffic rerouted.

Maya: FYI please update internal KB to include "egress pinning header" troubleshooting steps and add example curl with header.

Raj: Collected proxy logs + NAT mapping; diag bundle uploaded: https://internal.redwood/diag/8f4c/2187659999 (internal). Asking network ops to approve emergency rollback.

Tess: Rolling back peering-policy-2026-03-12 now (holding for safety window) — will monitor edge health.

Leah: Thanks. I'll let the customer know we have an active rollback + ETA ~45m and ask them to check latency after that. :thumbsup:

Maya: Postmortem items: clarify behavior of route hints vs header overrides and document quick-remediation playbook for customers who can't patch immediately.

Leah: I'll keep thread updated.
